page: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture with 22 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1880 GB NVMe SSD, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The instance excels in specialized tasks, achieving top 25% results in Geekbench ray tracing, image processing, and Passmark CPU encryption. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient, though large block read and write operations perform at an average level. For machine learning workloads, the NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing and text generation for small and medium models. However, a notable performance tradeoff occurs with large 70B models, where text generation speed drops to the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the g6.16xlarge offers a balanced allocation of compute, memory, and local NVMe storage alongside dedicated GPU acceleration, making it a cost-efficient option for mid-range AI and machine learning workloads without requiring multi-GPU overhead. The instance is highly suited for graphics-intensive applications, real-time ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. It is also well-suited for deploying small-to-medium scale LLM inference pipelines, though alternative hardware configurations should be considered for large-scale model text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 64 vCPUs and 256 GB of DDR4 memory, it features a dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM and a local 1880 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers strong multi-core CPU performance and high-speed memory bandwidth for cached blocks. Benchmark results highlight top-tier performance in LLM inference for small and medium models, alongside strong capabilities in ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. However, text generation for large 70B models represents a performance tradeoff, falling into the lower tier. This instance is highly suited for mid-range AI inference, graphics rendering, and compute-heavy database workloads.
